title: DR1 offers each address role only the addresses saved for that role; the frontend offers the whole address book on all five party pages and on the contact page.

finding.frontend: All five party pages show the same list. Place of origin, Consignor or exporter, Consignee, Importer and Place of destination each report "Showing 5 of 13 addresses" over the identical thirteen records, so a user choosing a place of origin is offered Tech Imports Ltd and Import Co UK alongside the farms, and a user choosing a consignee is offered Astra Rosales in Switzerland. The contact page offers the same book again, all thirteen as radios, including overseas addresses. This is deliberate today: the address book holds no type, so one search serves every role (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:12-15) and no picker passes a role to it (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/party-picker.controller.js:35-36).
finding.prototype: DR1 records what an address is for when it is saved, and each page shows only the matching records. The place-of-origin capture reports "Showing 9 out of 9 results" and every row is a farm or breeding centre abroad — the whole list is filtered against the role's type aliases (app/routes.js:3441-3465). Consignor or exporter also accepts records typed consignor or exporter; consignee, importer and place of destination each take their own type. The contact page is filtered separately, to addresses typed as a branch address, and DR1 seeds it with three GB branches of the trader's own business rather than with consignment addresses.
finding.difference: This needs the address book to carry what each address is for before the frontend can filter on it. The API's address contract has no such field — OperatorResponse in the address-book service exposes name, address lines, country, phone, email and the soft-delete flag and nothing role-shaped — so the contract, the store and the INS frontend's add form all have to gain it first. Only then can each party page ask for its own role and the contact page ask for branch addresses. Do the five party roles and the contact page in one pass: they read the same book through the same service and would otherwise diverge.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding two frontend party pages whose result counts differ, or a consignee page that omits an address the place-of-origin page offers.

relatedTo.why: an address saved from inside the journey has to be given a role at the point it is saved, which is the same field this finding needs
